findings.title: Session reschedule due to coach illness — explicitly not a product issue
findings.description: Eleanor reports one scheduling mixup during the period: a coach had to reschedule a session due to personal illness. She explicitly characterizes this as 'just life, not a product problem' and notes the rescheduling process itself went smoothly. No platform defect, app issue, or scheduling-tool failure is implicated.
findings.quote: The one time there was a mixup it was a coach who had to reschedule due to illness, which is just life, not a product problem
findings.severity_reason: Customer explicitly states this is not a product problem and the process worked fine; no defect to size.
findings.match_note: No catalogue issue applies; explicitly disclaimed as non-product by the customer herself, distinct from PROJ-138 (Outlook ICS timing bug) which is a different, unretracted defect not mentioned here.

findings.title: Request to extend coaching program to Project Managers (new user cohort)
findings.description: Eleanor is considering extending the coaching program to roughly 25 Project Managers across three studios, a group currently excluded from the program, and has asked the CSM (Derek) to draft a proposal for a PM-specific coaching track tailored to delivery/client management rather than design leadership. This is a request to expand the scope of the coaching service/program to a new employee segment, not a defect in or missing capability of the BetterBark software product itself. Timeline is not urgent (next month, ahead of fall budget cycle).
findings.quote: They're a different discipline entirely, often not architects at all, and they've been asking why coaching is only for the design side.
findings.severity_reason: Business/program expansion request handled via services proposal, not a product engineering item; no product functionality is broken or absent.
findings.match_note: No catalogue match; not a product feature gap (e.g., not comparable to PROJ-118 dashboard export) but a request to widen the coaching program's target audience, which is a services/account decision.
